source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Exodus 32–34.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves pronoun for disputed proclamation subject, with note relating natural LORD reading and possible Moses invocation.
Retains doubled name and ordered divine qualities, links hesed to faithful love in 20:6, and lineates proclamation within verse paragraph.
Keeps unqualified thousands, three wrongdoing terms, emphatic nonacquittal and intergenerational divine reckoning; no added limiting clause or softened natural-consequences paraphrase.
Takes ki concessively while noting causal alternative; preserves communal confession and inheritance request rather than separating Moses from people.
Keeps covenant making, created-wonders language, universal comparison and fear-inducing divine work without merely positive spectacle.
Retains covenant term for prohibited local pact and concrete snare image without broadening beyond stated inhabitants.
Retains destructive commands and three different cult objects; keeps Asherah identity with concise vocabulary rather than generic trees.
Preserves doubled divine jealousy and name claim without replacing with protective love or human insecurity commentary.
Retains sexual-infidelity metaphor and invitation-to-sacrifice sequence without asserting literal cult prostitution.
Preserves specific daughters/sons marriage direction and repeated prostitution metaphor as religious allegiance, not generic intermarriage ban.
Preserves opening-womb image and male specification of livestock with note acknowledging difficult compressed Hebrew form.
Preserves redemption, explicit animal harm, all firstborn sons, and appearance requirement; seh rendered sheep or goat consistent with its range.
Retains explicit male attendance, three times and layered divine titles, using the same Lord GOD convention as 23:17, without expanding participants to all genders.
Preserves divine displacement and territorial expansion, coveting rather than only invasion, and repeated attendance count.
Retains duration, complete abstention and ambiguous he wrote rather than silently naming writer; uses literal Ten Words with familiar-title note.
Retains unawareness, two tablets, actual skin and radiance; names the LORD as conversation partner and notes that the Hebrew can also describe God speaking with Moses.
